decision_clause: Ruled out: a hand-maintained product-code allowlist per ticket — because "each of the 60 remaining tickets would need a coordinated census amendment, and the list drifts from the tickets it mirrors." Scope covers scripts/validate-planning.mjs, tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs, packages/schema/{package.json,src/metric-registry.ts,test/metric-registry.test.ts}, specs/metrics.v0.json; lifecycle active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: diff.patch is 0 bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree, so no new admission list of any kind was introduced. In the finished tree, scripts/validate-planning.mjs still computes which source files are admitted by parsing each ticket document at read time — it opens every ticket file, extracts the `## Exact ownership` section, splits each bullet on `;` then on the em-dash to take the path side, and adds the `- Test file: \`...\`` RED path — accumulating them into `ticketOwnedPaths` (lines ~834-857). Any tracked source file with a code extension that no ticket claims fails closed with `unallowlisted product code` (line 868). The only literal path set in the file is `controlPlaneAllowlist` (17 entries, lines 809-827), which enumerates validator/harness files, not per-ticket product code, and is subtracted before the ticket-derived check rather than standing in for it. tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs independently re-derives the same census from the skeleton and asserts equality against the validator's reported `ticket_owned_code_paths`, so the two parses cannot silently diverge. packages/schema/src/metric-registry.ts contains no path or ticket admission list at all; its literal tables (FACTOR_OF, FROZEN_PRECEDENCE, FROZEN_CONFIDENCE, CANONICAL_IDS) encode the frozen M01-M20 scoring contract, and its consumer handling only requires `consumers` to be non-empty and every declared `consumer_routes` entry to appear in it — it reads the consumer set from the registry data rather than mirroring tickets.
rationale: The recorded decision forbids replacing the derived census with a per-ticket, hand-edited list of product-code paths, on the grounds that such a list would need amending alongside each of the 60 remaining tickets and would drift from them. The finished tree does the opposite of that on every scope path: the admission set is recomputed from the ticket documents on each run, and validate-planning.mjs even states in-line that "There is no standing product-code allowlist to edit, and unowned source still fails closed." No hardcoded ticket→path map was added anywhere in scope. The point is doubly settled here because diff.patch is empty — the implementation changed nothing, so it could not have introduced the ruled-out mechanism. Two things I checked and deliberately did not count as violations. First, `controlPlaneAllowlist` is a literal set of 17 file paths, i.e. a hand-maintained allowlist in the ordinary sense — but it is scoped to control-plane/validator files, is not keyed to tickets, and does not grow per ticket, so it is not the per-ticket product-code allowlist the decision names; it is also pre-existing and untouched. Second, the task itself asks for a hardcoded 9-member `consumers` set in the validator, which superficially reads as "a hardcoded allowlist in product code" — but it is a frozen scoring-contract envelope, not a census of which ticket owns which file, so it would not be the ruled-out approach even if implemented, and in fact it is not implemented: metric-registry.ts checks only `consumers.length === 0` and never compares `registry_id` or `source_contract` against their frozen values. That is a gap against the task, not against the decision, and the judgement asked here is only about the decision. Approving this tree would not require anyone to re-explain why the hand-maintained per-ticket allowlist was rejected, since the mechanism it rejected is absent and the derived alternative is intact.
